Mapping cylinder

Words: 19
Algebraic topology OurBigBook.com
The mapping cylinder of f:A→X is
Mf​=(A×[0,1]⊔X)/((a,0)∼f(a)).
(1)
It deformation retracts onto the copy of X.

Real projective space (RPn)

Words: 80 Articles: 3
Algebraic topology OurBigBook.com
Real projective space is the antipodal quotient RPn=Sn/(x∼−x).

Mapping-cylinder model of punctured real projective three-space

Words: 28
Real projective space OurBigBook.com
The complement of an open three-ball in RP3 is the mapping cylinder of the antipodal covering S2→RP2. It deformation retracts to RP2 and has boundary S2.

Integral homology of real projective three-space

Words: 14
Real projective space OurBigBook.com
The integral homology groups are
Hi​(RP3;Z)=⎩⎨⎧​Z,Z/2,0,​i=0,3,i=1,otherwise.​
(2)

Double of punctured real projective three-space

Words: 29
Real projective space OurBigBook.com
Doubling RP3 minus an open ball along its spherical boundary gives RP3#RP3. Its fundamental group is
(Z/2)∗(Z/2)≅D∞​,
(3)
and its universal cover is S2×R.

Homology

Words: 516 Articles: 22
Algebraic topology OurBigBook.com
Homology assigns abelian groups Hi​(X) to a space, measuring cycles modulo boundaries in each dimension.

Exact sequence

Words: 16
Homology OurBigBook.com
An exact sequence has the image of each map equal to the kernel of the next.

Commutative diagram

Words: 24
Homology OurBigBook.com
A commutative diagram is a diagram of objects and morphisms in which every two directed paths with the same endpoints define the same morphism.

PSL2(R) is SL2​(R)/{±I}. It acts on the upper half-plane by the Möbius transformations
z⟼cz+daz+b​
(136)
and is the group of orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometries.

Hyperbolic reflection

Words: 29
Poincare half-plane model OurBigBook.com
Reflection in a hyperbolic line is the unique orientation-reversing hyperbolic isometry fixing that line pointwise. The product of reflections in intersecting lines is a rotation through twice their angle.

Hyperbolic half-turn

Words: 32
Poincare half-plane model OurBigBook.com
A hyperbolic half-turn is the unique orientation-preserving isometry of order two fixing a given point. It exchanges every pair of points lying at equal opposite distances along a geodesic through its centre.

Cayley transform

Words: 15
Hyperbolic geometry OurBigBook.com
The map z↦i(1+z)/(1−z) is an isometry from the Poincare disc to the upper half-plane.

Hyperboloid model

Words: 50 Articles: 1
Hyperbolic geometry OurBigBook.com
The hyperboloid model of the curvature-minus-one hyperbolic plane is
{x∈R3:−x02​+x12​+x22​=−1,x0​>0}.
(137)
Its metric is the restriction of the Minkowski bilinear form to tangent planes, and its geodesics are intersections with two-dimensional linear subspaces through the origin.

Minkowski inner product

Words: 13
Hyperboloid model OurBigBook.com
On Rn+1 the Minkowski inner product with mostly-positive convention is
⟨x,y⟩M​=−x0​y0​+x1​y1​+⋯+xn​yn​.
(138)

Lambert quadrilateral

Words: 33
Hyperbolic geometry OurBigBook.com
A Lambert quadrilateral is a hyperbolic quadrilateral with three right angles. If its remaining angle is θ and the two sides incident with that angle have lengths a,b, then
cosθ=tanhatanhb.
(139)

Hyperbolic triangle

Words: 74 Articles: 4
Hyperbolic geometry OurBigBook.com
A hyperbolic triangle is bounded by three hyperbolic geodesics and may have vertices on the ideal boundary.

Ideal vertex

Words: 14
Hyperbolic triangle OurBigBook.com
An ideal vertex lies on the boundary at infinity and has internal angle zero.

Hyperbolic triangle area

Words: 35 Articles: 1
Hyperbolic triangle OurBigBook.com
For curvature −1, a triangle of angles α,β,γ has area π−α−β−γ by Gauss--Bonnet.
Hyperbolic polygon area
Words: 21
Hyperbolic triangle area OurBigBook.com
For a geodesic hyperbolic n-gon of curvature −1 with interior angles α1​,…,αn​, triangulation or the Gauss--Bonnet theorem gives
area=(n−2)π−∑j=1n​αj​.
(140)

For opposite side a, cosha=(cosα+cosβcosγ)/(sinβsinγ).
